thread:
kevin: ALB started deregistering a bunch of targets in ap-southeast-1 around 01:30 UTC. edge-syd target group went from ~250 -> ~40. Healthcheck failures reported. Anyone seeing this? :rotating_light:
rohit: I'm oncall, looking now. Is this only the edge cluster in syd? Which TG/ALB name?
kevin: It's `app-edge-alb-prod-1`, target type = ip (pods). Kube readiness still shows pods Ready on the node side. LB events show timeouts. Sample ALB event:```Target response codes: 504, target timed out after 10 seconds. 5 failed checks in a row.```
anita: please check node conntrack / NAT gateway. Last similar incident was ephemeral port exhaustion causing LB connections to fail vs nodes.
liz: I ran quick checks from bastion -> node pool. `ss -s` shows lots of TIME_WAIT and some SYN_RECV. Checked conntrack count via `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` — it's very high (~63k). Nodes are hitting conntrack limit on a few primaries. NAT gateway shows high connections/second too.
kevin: interesting — readiness probe is HTTP GET /ready on nodePort 30080. ALB does new TCP connection per check (no keepalive). That could create a new NAT entry each time. `ss -tan sport = :30080` on node shows many short-lived sockets.
infra-bot: autoscaler: requested scale up for nodepool edge-syd-heavy, adding 6 nodes (estimate).
rohit: OK plan: 1) temporarily increase target group healthcheck interval (reduce churn) 2) check conntrack max on current AMIs and bump sysctl if safe 3) consider switching TG target type to instance or enable proxy-protocol so ALB IP reuse reduces NAT churn. Any objections?
anita: +1. Also open ticket with cloud for NAT gateway connection limit in this region; we may be hitting per-NAT allocation.
liz: quick mitigation applied: increased target group interval from 5s -> 15s and healthy threshold from 5 -> 3 to shorten time to recover. Also raised net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max from 65536 -> 262144 on a couple of nodes as test. Watching.
kevin: after change the deregistrations stopped and targets are slowly re-registering. Still seeing high TIME_WAIT but connection rate dropped ~70%.
rohit: moving to next steps: schedule a safe AMI update to persist conntrack sysctl via boot config, and evaluate switching pod target type to instance-backed targets for this TG to avoid per-pod NAT churn. I'll follow up with a runbook entry.
kevin: thanks everyone. Filing quick postmortem and adding runbook notes. tagging for visibility. :memo:
deploy-bot: deployment webhook: no recent deploys to edge-syd in the last 2 hours.
liz: adding note — long term: consider giving ALB an ENI in the VPC with proxy-protocol or using NLB with preserved source IP for high-frequency healthchecks. Also evaluate HTTP keepalive on healthcheck path.
kevin: resolved for now, will keep monitoring for 2h and then close incident. :white_check_mark:
